main_topics.reason: The user described pain in both hands, morning stiffness, and episodes of whole-finger swelling as the main signs prompting the conversation.
The user asked what psoriatic arthritis is and whether waiting could lead to permanent joint damage.
The user described nail pitting and lifting and returned to ask about improving the nail that looked bad.
The user asked which doctor to see and said they would request a referral through their health plan.
The user asked what to expect at the appointment because they dislike not knowing what will happen.
The user asked whether a blood test could confirm the suspected condition.
The user asked what they could take for pain and mentioned sometimes using dipyrone.
The user asked whether anything could be done for the affected nail and whether arthritis treatment could help it.
The user said the possibility of arthritis and lasting damage scared them, then reported feeling better after understanding the plan.

output.summary: The user described psoriasis, nail pitting and lifting, and painful, stiff, sometimes swollen fingers, and asked whether this could be psoriatic arthritis and whether it could cause permanent damage. The assistant explained the suspected condition, referral and appointment process, testing, and symptom and nail treatment; the user said they felt better, understood the possibility, and planned to ask their dermatologist for a referral that week.
